text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government, workers' union agree to raise minimum wage to 6,000 dinars ($107) from 4,000 ($71); increase will be in three stages starting in May.
- Train bomb kills 21 passengers, wounds 20 near Algiers.
- Air Algerie resumes flights to Paris; national airline stopped flights to French capital in 1995 in dispute with aviation authorities over security measures.
- President Zeroual meets Salah Boubnider, head of independent poll watchdog, pledges government will help committee supervise parliamentary elections.
- Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker, U.N. secretary-general's personal representative for Western Sahara, meets Algerian officials before talks with Polisario leaders.
